correctness.rationale: For each m>=2, generic symmetric data reduce the projector-objective critical problem to the spectral curve G(t,mu)=0 of bidegree (2,m+1). A smooth genus-m curve arises from an explicit arrowhead specialization with 2m+2 simple branch points. The critical-value function h=mu+alpha(t) has exactly 2m simple poles above t=±i and no poles at the two mu=infinity corners. Riemann--Hurwitz gives 2m-2+4m=6m-2 ramification. The proof also checks nonramification at excluded corners, at simple poles and spectral fold points; a generic smooth linear-Morse condition excludes other boundary losses. Independently checked arrowhead specializations m=2..5 with squarefree branch polynomials and the 6m−2 count; this finite check is not the all-m proof.
